fields.meta_title: Landing Page SEO: How to Build Pages That Rank | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Landing page SEO in seven steps, then prompt Emergent for the title tag and schema of a page you own, plus a lead form. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build Landing Page SEO Into Pages That Rank and Convert
fields.hero_description: Name the query and describe the offer. Emergent builds the page with the title tag and schema markup your prompt asks for, plus a lead form, as code you own.
fields.features_heading: What to Ask for in an SEO Landing Page
fields.features_subheading: Landing page SEO means ranking one page for the query its buyers search, and turning each organic visit into a lead.
fields.feature_1:
Title tag and H1 written around the query

Name the query in your prompt and Emergent writes the title tag and H1 around it. If Search Console shows impressions but few clicks, one more prompt rewords the title.
fields.feature_2:
Sections that follow search intent

Tell Emergent what the searcher came for and the page opens on that answer, with an H2 for each question they ask next. Prompt for the lead form below the first answer.
fields.feature_3:
Structured data and canonical tags

Ask for Product or LocalBusiness schema and Emergent writes it into the page as JSON-LD. Name a canonical URL and a sitemap entry in the same prompt, and both go in.
fields.feature_4:
A phone layout you can test and tune

Ask for a responsive layout with alt text and fixed image sizes, then run the published page through PageSpeed Insights. Each issue it flags is one more prompt to fix.
fields.feature_5:
Leads saved with their landing URL

Ask for the form to save each submission to a database you own with its landing URL and referrer, then send it to HubSpot or Slack. Organic leads stay apart from paid.
fields.feature_6:
Markup you can audit and keep

Export the page and its lead form to your GitHub repository as plain code. Run any crawler against it, hand it to a developer, or host it elsewhere without a rebuild.

fields.usecase_heading: SEO Landing Pages for Four Kinds of Query
fields.tab_content_1:
Aim a feature page at the query buyers type

A feature page targets one commercial query, such as shift scheduling software. Prompt for the query in the title tag, H1 and URL, and add a demo form below the opening answer. Each demo request is saved with its landing URL.
fields.tab_content_2:
Publish one page per city, each with its own copy

City pages target searches like movers in Denver. Prompt for a page per branch, each with its own H1, service area and LocalBusiness schema, and no two pages read alike. Quote requests are saved with the city attached and posted to that branch's Slack channel.
fields.tab_content_3:
Answer the comparison search with a fair table

Comparison pages answer queries like Acme vs Globex or Globex alternatives. Ask for the differences in a table with Breadcrumb schema, plus links to the feature pages it mentions. The trial signup at the end records which comparison the visitor read.
fields.tab_content_4:
Turn a template search into a captured lead

Template pages target queries like content calendar template. The page previews the template and explains how to fill it in. Ask for an email before the download, and each lead is stored with its source page while the contact is created in HubSpot.

fields.howto_title: How to Build an SEO Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Pick one query and study what already ranks for it. Write the page around that query, check it on a phone before launch, and judge it by the leads it brings in.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Match what the top results deliver
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Put the query in the title and H1
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Answer before you ask for anything
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose the single query the page should rank for and check that the top results are pages like yours. If the first page of Google is all guides, a sales page will struggle there; write a guide-shaped page or pick another query.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open the top ten and note the format they share and the questions they answer. A commercial query wants pricing and proof near the top. An informational one wants the definition first and the offer after it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Lead the title tag with the query, worded the way people search it, and repeat it in the H1. Keep the URL short and readable. Write a meta description that says what the page delivers, not a slogan.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Cover the topic at the depth the search needs, starting with a plain answer in the first two lines. Put the form after that answer. Visitors and crawlers should both reach the content before they reach the ask.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Add the structured data that fits the page type: Product for a feature page, LocalBusiness for a city page. Give every image descriptive alt text. Link to the page from related pages on your site, with anchor text that names its topic.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test the page on a phone
fields.howto_step_6_des: Load the page on a mid-range phone and run it through PageSpeed Insights. Compress the hero image and set its dimensions. Defer any script the first screen does not need, and fix layout shift before you publish.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish on your domain and submit the URL in Google Search Console. Each week, compare the query's impressions with its clicks and form conversions. When clicks lag the position, rewrite the title tag.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build Landing Page SEO Into Pages That Rank and Convert', title 'Landing Page SEO: How to Build Pages That Rank' and hero 'Describe the offer and the query it should rank for...' cover ranking plus conversion, the whole job, not a sibling's topic.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is mostly guides (Semrush, Search Engine Land, Instapage blog); the page delivers a 7-step how-to ('Pick one query per page' ... 'Publish, submit and measure'), a checklist answer and four page-type examples. Off-topic PAA drift is judged under faq.

specificity.evidence: why_table Emergent 'How you build' cell reads 'Prompt for a campaign page': hub boilerplate (CONTENT_DEFECTS #3) and a sibling's topic (campaign landing page) on a page about organic ranking. Fix in rules/competitors/lp.json: an seo-variant build cell (e.g. 'Prompt for a page built to rank for one query'), then regenerate the table; needs library sign-off.

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: 'Name the query and Emergent writes the title tag...', 'City pages target searches like movers in Denver.', 'Choose the single query the page should rank for...'.

craft.evidence: Sentences carry one idea and end on the key word ('Organic leads stay separate from paid.', 'Fix layout shift before you publish.'); longest list sentence (checklist FAQ, 27 words) is under the 32-word flag.

voice.evidence: Body copy holds up, but several FAQ lines read as keyword insertion or aphorism, not a writer: 'For landing pages for SEO, it means...', 'each landing page for SEO ranks for a specific problem', 'A search engine optimization landing page you have rewritten three times is a better teacher than a checklist.' howto_description ends on a summary line: 'Seven steps from keyword to an indexed page that converts.' Rewrite so each secondary sits where a person would say it, and cut the aphorism and summary.

truth.evidence: SEO defaults are stated as automatic platform behavior with no ledger id in claims_used (only prompt-build, api-connect, code-export, database-owned, custom-domain, free-start): 'Each page gets a canonical tag and a sitemap entry', 'The layout is responsive from the first build', 'scripts load after the content', 'each sized to show in full on a results page' (Google truncates by pixel and rewrites titles; not a guarantee). Images show 'Indexed' / 'Page indexed', implying Emergent confirms Google indexing. Unsupported generalizations (CONTENT_DEFECTS #7): 'Search Console data from your own site teaches more than most courses', 'SEO friendly landing pages that answer the query in their opening lines are easier for those summaries to quote.' Fix: frame SEO features as what the prompt asks the build to include (or get a ledger entry from Divit), change 'Indexed' to a state Emergent can know (e.g. 'Published' / 'In sitemap'), and cut or soften the generalizations.

distinct.evidence: Organised around query types ('Feature Pages', 'City Pages', 'Comparison Pages', 'Template Pages') and on-page SEO steps; no sibling primary in headings; QC D2 clean against the hub.

faq.evidence: Three QC-F4-forced drift items do not serve someone searching 'landing page seo' (CONTENT_DEFECTS #9): 'What is SEO expert salary?' is also not answered in its first sentence ('It depends on location, seniority...so check current listings'); 'How long will it take me to learn SEO?' and 'Can I learn SEO on my own?' are career questions with landing pages bolted on. Secondaries are forced in ('Search engine landing pages need unique copy', 'For landing pages for SEO'). Reviewer view: these three PAA items should be filtered as drift (F4 filter should require topic overlap beyond the single token 'seo'); replace with on-topic sources (related 'Landing page seo template', 'Types of landing page', keyword 'seo landing page design'). If Divit keeps F4 as is, the salary answer must still open with an answer.

images.evidence: Each tab shows one moment matching its copy: Aurora quote 'City: Aurora' in #aurora-branch (tab 2 'posted to that branch's Slack channel'), 'Read: Acme vs Globex' (tab 3 'records which comparison the visitor read'), 'Contact created in HubSpot' (tab 4); cursor on button edges; balance gate passed. Minor: tab 1 email 'dana@globex.com' reuses tab 3's competitor brand; 'Indexed' badges flagged under truth.
